claims.text: An adaptive machine-learning interatomic potential with periodic on-the-fly DFT corrections can accurately evaluate solid and liquid free energies near fusion.
The hybrid method will retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling effects.
The hybrid method will reduce computational cost by approximately 10× relative to explicit AIMD.
The hybrid method will provide a 2–5× speed improvement over TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
Sparse, strategically selected DFT free-energy evaluations are sufficient to train the adaptive ML potential across solid–liquid phase boundaries.
Periodic DFT corrections can capture anharmonic, vibrational, and electron–vibration coupling effects across phase boundaries.
The proposed method is applicable from near the melting temperature to approximately 1.5 times the melting temperature.
The proposed method is applicable to pure elements, binary alloys, and multicomponent systems containing up to five components.
Continual ML-IAP updating with DFT corrections will accurately map the relevant free-energy surface.
ML-based sampling will screen out most expensive explicit molecular-dynamics sampling while maintaining fidelity.
Rapid ML sampling combined with intermittent DFT correction will reproduce physically relevant free-energy differences between solid and liquid phases without full AIMD.
The method will predict phase free energies, melting temperatures, and latent heats within approximately 5–10% of explicit AIMD results.
Explicit AIMD free-energy calculations and established TOR-TILD results for elemental and binary systems can serve as reference baselines.
Systems with extreme anharmonicity or strong electron–vibration coupling may require additional validation.
Strong anharmonicity or rapidly varying free-energy landscapes may increase the required frequency of DFT corrections and reduce computational savings.
Deviation greater than approximately 10% from explicit AIMD or experimental benchmarks is a falsification threshold.
A computational speed-up of less than 2× relative to TOR-TILD in multicomponent systems is a falsification threshold.
